Backend 22/22 pass on new test_iter83_boxanim.py (18 valid keys accepted+persisted, unknown rejected with 'Unknown box entrance animation', empty '' clears override, GET returns box_anim + options.box_anims of length 18, public /public/site/{token} carries the tenant's chosen box_anim). Regression 36/36 green on iter80+81+82. Frontend on /p/pv_c3b797fcdafc58d4e70e320f (app_testlab): 44 .cm-box elements tagged, 0 .cm-box.absolute/fixed leaks, 0 nested .cm-box inside .cm-box, all 44 uniformly carry the same cm-a-<key> class. Switching the API override to bounce/spin/pulse/'' via PUT flips the class on the next public load (verified all four transitions). IntersectionObserver replay works in both directions: cm-in toggles false→true (enter) → false (out of view) → true again on re-entry, and getAnimations() reports a live animation both times. Site Mode picker (SiteModePanel): [data-testid=sm-boxanim-select] is a <select> with 19 values ('' + 18 keys, all matching backend BOX_ANIMS). Preview renders 3 dummy boxes carrying cm-a-<chosen>, sm-boxanim-replay button toggles them and works. Reduced-motion: ContentMotion short-circuits so no .cm-box classes are added and the CSS kill-switch keeps content fully visible with no animation/clip-path. Mobile 390px: 44 boxes tagged, no horizontal overflow, no absolute leaks.

ui_bugs.issue: CSS specificity conflict: `.dsv2 .tstagger-in.tstagger > *` (specificity 0,3,1) declares `animation: tfadeup .65s ...` and OVERRIDES `.cm-a-<key>.cm-in { animation-name: cma-<key>; }` (specificity 0,2,0). Verified live: a .tcard element with class `tcard cm-a-bounce cm-in` reports computed animationName='tfadeup' duration=0.65s, whereas a sibling H2 with `cm-a-bounce cm-in` correctly reports animationName='cma-bounce' duration=0.9s. Net effect: every card on every tenant site keeps the old tfadeup entrance regardless of box_anim / TEMPLATE_ANIM, breaking the user's core requirement that each template (and each tenant's Site Mode choice) actually change what the boxes do. Only headings/standalone paragraphs animate with the new PowerPoint keyframes.

Selecting a value in sm-boxanim-select emitted a red toast 'Could not save Site Mode' during rapid interaction (same rate-limit family observed in iter82 during rapid iframe refetches). The API accepts the value fine when called directly. Consider a debounced save or a longer client-side retry.

action_items: Fix the tcard/tfadeup override in /app/frontend/src/styles/tenant-v2.css: either scope tfadeup off .cm-box, bump the .cm-a-*.cm-in rules with an ancestor selector like `.dsv2 .cm-box.cm-a-<key>.cm-in { animation-name: cma-<key> !important; }`, or move the ContentMotion CSS after tenant-v2.css and add a specificity boost such as `.cm-box.cm-a-<key>.cm-in.cm-a-<key> { animation-name: cma-<key>; }`. Without this fix the entire feature is invisible on cards.
Debounce or coalesce the Site Mode box_anim save to avoid the 'Could not save Site Mode' toast under rapid selection changes.
critical_code_review_comments: ContentMotion.tsx line 108-111: standalone `section > div` and `section > blockquote` get tagged as their own group after the .grid children pass. Filter `.closest('.cm-box')` prevents nesting, but the wrapper `section > div` that CONTAINS the grid of cards may still get tagged BEFORE the grid pass (order is grid-children first, then standalone) — so the check `!el.querySelector('.cm-box')` protects against this. Verified: 0 nested leaks in the wild. Correct.

boxAnims.ts TEMPLATE_ANIM has 33 templates but only 15 unique animation values — several templates intentionally share (hvac==hvac_plumbing='fly-in', fitness==pet_grooming='bounce', construction==accounting==architecture='wipe', hospitality==wellness='fade', creative_studio==landscaping='shape', logistics==automotive='wheel', retail==photography='zoom', it_services==cleaning='random-bars', saas==coworking='grow-turn', education==music_school='swivel', real_estate==nonprofit='grow-shrink', restaurant==beauty='pulse', finance==insurance='split', dental==healthcare='float-in'). The user requirement was 'each template has one unique animation' — clarify whether this pairing is intentional or if all 33 must be individually unique (would need >18 keyframes).

case_study.py put_site_mode: `box_anim` validation only runs when `patch.get('box_anim')` is truthy, so empty string '' passes through and clears the override (intended). Confirmed by test_empty_string_clears_override.

ContentMotion.tsx safety-net at 1.4s only ADDS cm-in to boxes on screen — good — but a slow-streaming block that mounts after 1.4s and above the fold could theoretically stay invisible until the user scrolls. In practice tag() runs at 60ms and 700ms so this is unlikely.

rca of the issue: PowerPoint animation feature is wired correctly end-to-end (backend accepts+persists+returns; frontend tags cm-box + cm-a-<key>; observer replays cm-in on scroll). However on production tenant pages the pre-existing tenant-v2.css rule `.dsv2 .tstagger-in.tstagger > * { animation: tfadeup .65s ...; }` has specificity (0,3,1) which beats the ContentMotion rule `.cm-a-<key>.cm-in { animation-name: cma-<key>; }` at (0,2,0). Therefore every .tcard keeps the old fade-up animation and none of the 17 new keyframes ever run on cards, only on headings/paragraphs. Reproduction: PUT /api/apps/app_testlab/site-mode {box_anim:'bounce'} → open /p/pv_c3b797fcdafc58d4e70e320f → getComputedStyle on any .tcard.cm-box.cm-a-bounce.cm-in reports animationName='tfadeup'. Mitigation: raise specificity of ContentMotion rules (e.g. add a body-level class selector or `!important` on animation-name/duration), OR scope the tenant-v2 tstagger rule to `:not(.cm-box)`, OR unset animation on `.cm-box` inside .dsv2 stagger containers.
